newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INL yet to close Sky TV deal.
newsitem.headline: INL yet to close Sky TV deal.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Ltd said on Monday negotiations to purchase a stake in pay TV operator Sky Network Television were still ongoing, but difficult issues relating to shareholding structure had to be resolved if the investment were to go ahead.
In October last year INL said it was negotiating with a group of companies that together own more than 80 percent of Sky to buy a substantial stake.

Those companies include Heatley Jarvis Investments (15.8 percent), Todd Corporation (8.8 percent), Tappenden Construction (7.7 percent) and United States-based HKP Partners (51.1 percent). HKP is partly owned by Bell Atlantic and Ameritech, which in turn own half of Telecom Corp of New Zealand.
State-owned Television New Zealand holds the balance of Sky, which is not for sale.
INL had earlier hoped to announce the Sky deal by the end of December, but later set back any announcement to January because of "tedious detail".
INL is just under half owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation. Sky is not related to Murdoch's 40 percent-owned European-based satellite network BSkyB. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
